_comment: Deterministic shadow-replan fixtures. Each case is (proposal, replace_keys)
run against a plan seeded from OBJECTIVE on a known page. They exist so
the activation decision rests on reproducible inputs rather than on
whatever the model happened to produce during one live run.
page.elements/page.url/page.text describe the observation passed to the
evaluator. None of these cases is adopted; would_adopt() is read-only.
objective: Add two items to the cart, then complete checkout.

elements: View details for Sauce Labs Backpack
page.text: Products. Add to cart. Cart, empty.

cases.name: historical_failure_checkout_replaced_by_visible_controls
cases.why: The regression this layer exists for: the planner restated controls already on screen, so the plan looked complete while checkout was never reached.

cases.name: plausible_reroute_accepted
cases.why: A route toward a page that does not exist yet is a real next step. The guard must be discriminating, not blanket.

cases.name: unrelated_work_displaces_outstanding_requirement
cases.why: Documents the known limitation: replace_keys is trusted, so a proposal naming unrelated non-filler work can displace outstanding work. Pinned so the gap stays visible.

cases.name: safety_violating_route_refused
cases.why: A proposal must not introduce a route the executor's safety boundary would refuse to cross later.
proposal: bypass the login then finish checkout

cases.name: quantity_contradiction_refused
cases.why: The objective says two items. A proposal may not quietly change the number the user asked for.
proposal: add three items to the cart
replace_keys: add two items to the cart

cases.name: plan_growth_measured
cases.why: Activation must know whether proposals inflate the plan, since every extra step consumes the step budget.

cases.name: no_proposal_at_all
cases.why: A failed planner call must be measured, not treated as an adoption.
